title: Agility Robotics becomes the first pure-play humanoid stock on Nasdaq
subtitle: The Churchill Capital XI SPAC closed November 4 and shares opened as AGLT on November 5. Gross proceeds came in at $465M — well below the $620M initially estimated, after 61.5% of Class A shareholders redeemed.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Agility Robotics began trading on Nasdaq as AGLT on November 5, following its SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI. Shareholders approved the deal on November 2, the transaction closed November 4, and the stock opened at $11.26 above the $10 SPAC reference price. The deal valued the company at about $2.5 billion. Gross proceeds totaled roughly $465 million — well below the more than $620 million originally anticipated when the merger was announced in June, after 61.5% of Class A shareholders redeemed. About $164 million came from Churchill XI's trust, $201 million from a PIPE led by Foxconn, and $100 million from a round closed after the SPAC announcement.

The 'first' matters in how you read it. Unitree, Figure, and Apptronik have each been rumored IPO candidates, and Chinese players like Xpeng Robotics and Unitree are in various IPO pipelines on the STAR Market and Hong Kong. Agility arriving first on a US exchange — via SPAC, with heavy redemptions, and with reported H1 2026 revenue of just $174,000 largely from related parties — says more about which pipeline moved first than about which company has the strongest business. For comparable context: the SPAC route and the redemption rate are the standard pattern for a company that wanted public currency before its revenue could support a traditional IPO.

The business behind the ticker is real. Agility's Digit robot has been deployed in warehouses with GXO Logistics, Amazon has been an investor, and the company has a product shipping into a market that hyperscalers are explicitly building for. But public-market investors now have a live price for a humanoid robotics company, and that price will reset expectations for every private comparable — Figure, Apptronik, 1X, Sanctuary — whether or not the comparison is fair. Expect that pressure to show up in their next funding rounds.

A takeaway for learners: a SPAC with heavy redemptions is a different animal from a conventional IPO. The company gets public currency; the pricing signal is noisier, the shareholder base is less sticky, and the initial trading range can be dominated by sponsor and PIPE unlock schedules rather than business fundamentals. If you are tracking humanoid robotics or embodied AI as an investment theme, read Agility's 10-Qs before pattern-matching from its stock price — the price will take months to find its real level.
